A DOG'S PERFECT CHRISTMAS officially releases tomorrow, November 4, on Netflix, bringing a brand new heartwarming holiday movie starring Dennis Quaid and Mary Steenburgen.

Based on the novel by W. Bruce Cameron, the bestselling author behind A DOG'S PURPOSE, the film follows a family whose Christmas plans fall apart after an unexpected medical emergency changes everything.

At the center of the story is Winstead, a loyal basset hound who tries to bring his struggling family back together before Christmas Eve, proving that sometimes the smallest members of a household can make the biggest difference.

The movie also stars Milo Ventimiglia, Jennifer Tilly, and Brooke Lena Johnson, with Thomas Haden Church providing the voice of Winstead. It marks another emotional dog-centered story from the author who brought audiences A DOG'S PURPOSE and A DOG'S JOURNEY.

Christmas movies are officially making their way back to Netflix, and A DOG'S PERFECT CHRISTMAS looks ready to deliver everything that makes the holidays special. Family, second chances, a little Christmas magic, and one very good dog holding everything together.

Netflix is once again testing a major redesign for its TV app. This new layout moves the main navigation menu back to the left-hand side of the screen, just months after the streamer rolled out a top-bar design globally. 

Beyond the sidebar, the test includes a layout that fits more titles on your screen at once, making it easier to scan through your watchlist. Video previews have also been moved to the top of the screen to free up space. This is currently only a test for select accounts, but it hints at where the Netflix experience is heading next.

माधव नेपाल र मिनेन्द्र रिजालसहित ९४ जनाविरुद्ध भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दा, ७६ करोड बिगो दाबी!

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री माधवकुमार नेपाल र नेपाली कांग्रेसका नेता तथा पूर्वमन्त्री डा. मिनेन्द्र रिजालसहितका व्यक्तिविरुद्ध भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दा दायर गरेको छ। सरकारी जग्गा गैरकानुनी रूपमा छुट दर्ता, सट्टापट्टा तथा बिक्री गरिएको आरोपमा अख्तियारले विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा अघि बढाएको हो।

मोरङको विराटनगर र सुनसरीको इटहरी क्षेत्रसँग जोडिएको रिजाल क्यानिङ कम्पनी तथा रिजाल टासी इन्डस्ट्रिजको जग्गा प्रकरणमा अनियमितता भएको अख्तियारको दाबी छ।

अख्तियारका अनुसार कम्पनीको नाममा रहेको हदबन्दीभन्दा बढी जग्गा मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयमार्फत सट्टापट्टा गर्न अनुमति दिइएको थियो। त्यसपछि मूल्यवान् जग्गा बिक्री गरी अन्य स्थानको जग्गासँग सट्टापट्टा गरिएको विषयमा अनुसन्धान गरिएको हो।

तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री माधवकुमार नेपाल नेतृत्वको मन्त्रिपरिषद्ले गरेको निर्णय र त्यसमा तत्कालीन मन्त्री मिनेन्द्र रिजालको भूमिकालाई समेत अनुसन्धानको दायरामा ल्याइएको छ।

मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयमाथि प्रश्न

यो प्रकरणमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्बाट भएको निर्णयका आधारमा सार्वजनिक जग्गा व्यक्तिको स्वामित्वमा गएको वा कम्पनीलाई गैरकानुनी लाभ पुगेको भन्ने विषयमा अख्तियारले प्रश्न उठाएको छ।

आरोपपत्रमा तत्कालीन सरकारी अधिकारी, भूमि प्रशासनसँग सम्बन्धित कर्मचारी तथा जग्गा कारोबारमा संलग्न व्यक्तिहरूको भूमिकाबारे समेत अनुसन्धान गरिएको छ।

मुद्दामा पूर्वमन्त्री डम्बर श्रेष्ठ, पूर्वसचिव छविराज पन्त तथा भूमि व्यवस्थासँग सम्बन्धित अन्य उच्चपदस्थ अधिकारीहरू पनि प्रतिवादीको सूचीमा रहेको समाचार सार्वजनिक भएको छ।

९४ जना र ७६ करोडको प्रारम्भिक विवरण

मुद्दा दायर भएको सुरुवाती समाचारहरूमा माधव नेपाल र मिनेन्द्र रिजालसहित ९४ जनालाई प्रतिवादी बनाउँदै करिब ७६ करोड रुपैयाँ बिगो दाबी गरिएको उल्लेख थियो।

तर पछि सार्वजनिक भएका विवरणमा प्रतिवादीको संख्या र बिगो रकम फरक देखिएको छ। अनलाइनखबर र नागरिक न्यूजले ९७ जना प्रतिवादी तथा करिब ७३ करोड ४९ लाख रुपैयाँ बिगो दाबी गरिएको विवरण प्रकाशित गरेका छन्।

यस मुद्दामा केही व्यक्तिलाई जग्गा जफत गर्ने प्रयोजनका लागि मात्र विपक्षी बनाइएको समेत उल्लेख छ।

अदालतबाट हुन बाँकी छ अन्तिम फैसला

माधवकुमार नेपाल र मिनेन्द्र रिजालविरुद्ध भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दा दायर भए पनि उनीहरू दोषी प्रमाणित भइसकेका छैनन्। अख्तियारले लगाएका आरोप, प्रस्तुत प्रमाण र प्रतिवादीहरूको जवाफको परीक्षणपछि विशेष अदालतले निर्णय गर्नेछ।

बेलायत जाने नेपालीका लागि दुःखको खबर! पीआर पाउन १० वर्ष कुर्नुपर्ने!

अध्ययन, रोजगारी तथा स्थायी बसोबासको सपना बोकेर बेलायत जाने तयारीमा रहेका नेपालीहरूका लागि महत्त्वपूर्ण खबर सार्वजनिक भएको छ। बेलायत सरकारले विदेशी नागरिकलाई स्थायी बसोबास अनुमति अर्थात् पीआर प्राप्त गर्न लाग्ने समय बढाउने नयाँ नीति अघि सारेको छ। यसअनुसार अधिकांश विदेशी कामदारले अब पाँच वर्षको सट्टा १० वर्ष कुर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था प्रस्ताव गरिएको छ।

बेलायतकी गृहमन्त्री शबाना महमुदले नोभेम्बर २ मा संसद्मा नयाँ अध्यागमन नीतिबारे जानकारी दिएकी हुन्। सरकारले यसलाई ‘अर्न्ड सेटलमेन्ट’ (Earned Settlement) नाम दिएको छ। यो व्यवस्थाअनुसार बेलायतमा कति वर्ष बसेको छ भन्ने मात्रै नभई व्यक्तिको आम्दानी, रोजगारी, आचरण तथा देशप्रतिको योगदानलाई पनि स्थायी बसोबासको आधार बनाइनेछ।

यसअघि बेलायतमा निश्चित प्रकारका कामदार भिसामा गएका विदेशी नागरिकले सामान्यतया पाँच वर्षपछि स्थायी बसोबासका लागि आवेदन दिन पाउने व्यवस्था थियो। तर नयाँ योजनाले अधिकांश कामदारका लागि उक्त अवधि दोब्बर बनाउनेछ।

सबैले १० वर्ष कुर्नुपर्ने भने होइन

बेलायत सरकारले सबै विदेशी नागरिकका लागि एउटै नियम लागू गर्ने भनेको छैन। वार्षिक ५० हजार पाउन्डभन्दा बढी आम्दानी भएका योग्य कामदार तथा डाक्टर, नर्स र शिक्षकजस्ता सार्वजनिक सेवाका केही कर्मचारीले पाँच वर्षमै स्थायी बसोबासका लागि आवेदन दिन सक्नेछन्।

त्यस्तै, वार्षिक एक लाख २५ हजार पाउन्डभन्दा बढी कमाउने उच्च आय भएका व्यक्तिले निश्चित सर्त पूरा गरे तीन वर्षमै स्थायी बसोबासको अवसर पाउन सक्नेछन्।

तर सामान्य आम्दानी भएका अधिकांश विदेशी कामदारले १० वर्ष कुर्नुपर्ने प्रस्ताव छ। अध्यागमन नियम उल्लङ्घन गर्ने व्यक्तिले भने अझ लामो समय कुर्नुपर्ने वा अनुमति नपाउन सक्ने व्यवस्था अघि सारिएको छ।

बेलायतमा रहेका नेपालीलाई कस्तो असर पर्छ?

बेलायतमा रोजगारी गरिरहेका तथा भविष्यमा त्यहाँ जाने तयारीमा रहेका नेपालीहरूलाई पनि नयाँ व्यवस्थाले असर पार्न सक्छ।

विशेषगरी सामान्य तलबमा काम गर्ने नेपालीहरूले स्थायी बसोबासका लागि पहिलेभन्दा लामो समय कुर्नुपर्ने अवस्था आउन सक्छ। यद्यपि, व्यक्तिको भिसाको प्रकार, पेशा, आम्दानी र अन्य योग्यताअनुसार फरक नियम लागू हुन सक्नेछन्।

बेलायत सरकारले यसअघि नै स्थायी बसोबास अनुमति प्राप्त गरिसकेका व्यक्तिको अधिकार नखोसिने स्पष्ट पारेको छ। साथै, केही स्वास्थ्य तथा हेरचाह सेवाका कामदार र बेलायतमा पहिल्यै बसोबास गरिरहेका व्यक्तिका लागि विशेष व्यवस्था पनि प्रस्ताव गरिएको छ।

सरकारी अनुमानअनुसार नयाँ नीतिका कारण पाँच लाखभन्दा बढी आप्रवासीले स्थायी बसोबास प्राप्त गर्न पहिलेभन्दा लामो समय कुर्नुपर्ने हुन सक्छ।

नयाँ नियम कहिलेदेखि लागू हुन्छ?

बेलायत सरकारले नयाँ नीति सार्वजनिक गरे पनि यसको विस्तृत कानुनी व्यवस्था र कार्यान्वयन प्रक्रिया अझै पूरा भएको छैन।

सरकारले डिसेम्बर २०२६ देखि अध्यागमन नियममा परिवर्तन अघि बढाउने र सन् २०२७ बाट चरणबद्ध रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्ने योजना सार्वजनिक गरेको छ।

नयाँ व्यवस्थाअनुसार स्थायी बसोबासका लागि आवेदन दिने व्यक्तिले आवश्यक अंग्रेजी भाषा ज्ञान, कानुनी आचरण, कर तथा राष्ट्रिय बीमामा योगदान र अन्य सरकारी मापदण्ड पूरा गर्नुपर्नेछ।

बेलायत सरकारले नयाँ नीतिले अध्यागमन प्रणालीलाई व्यवस्थित बनाउने र देशको अर्थतन्त्र तथा सार्वजनिक सेवामा योगदान गर्ने व्यक्तिलाई प्राथमिकता दिने दाबी गरेको छ।

सुरक्षाको चिन्ताबीच एसियाली खेलमा रोनाल्डो अनुपस्थित, प्रशिक्षकले दिए आराम!

पोर्चुगलका विश्वप्रसिद्ध फुटबलर क्रिस्टियानो रोनाल्डो एसियाली च्याम्पियन्स लिगअन्तर्गत उज्बेकिस्तानको पाख्ताकोरविरुद्धको खेलमा अनुपस्थित भएका छन्। मध्यपूर्वमा बढ्दो सुरक्षा चिन्ताका बीच साउदी अरेबियाको क्लब अल नासरका प्रशिक्षक एन्ज पोस्टेकोग्लुले रोनाल्डोलाई आराम दिने निर्णय गरेका हुन्।

नोभेम्बर २ मा उज्बेकिस्तानको राजधानी तास्कन्दमा भएको खेलका लागि रोनाल्डो टोलीसँग यात्रा गरेका थिएनन्। प्रशिक्षकले रोनाल्डोसँगै किङ्स्ले कोमान र मोहम्मद सिमाकानलाई पनि आराम दिएका थिए।

उत्तर कोरियाको सरकारी समाचार संस्था केसीएनएले मंगलबार सार्वजनिक गरेको विवरणअनुसार नोभेम्बर २ मा रणनीतिक क्रुज मिसाइलमा जडान गरिएको नयाँ क्लस्टर वारहेडको प्रभावकारिता परीक्षण गरिएको हो। परीक्षणको उद्देश्य नयाँ हतियारको क्षमता र मिसाइलको उडानसम्बन्धी विशेषता मूल्यांकन गर्नु रहेको बताइएको छ।

उत्तर कोरियाली मिसाइल प्रशासनअन्तर्गतको वारहेड अनुसन्धान संस्थानले नयाँ मध्यम आकारको क्लस्टर वारहेडले एकैपटक ठूलो क्षेत्र प्रभावित पार्न सक्ने दाबी गरेको छ। यद्यपि, उत्तर कोरियाले सार्वजनिक गरेको उक्त क्षमताको स्वतन्त्र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय पुष्टि भने भएको छैन।

क्लस्टर वारहेड यस्तो प्रकारको हतियार हो, जसले एउटै मिसाइलबाट धेरै साना विस्फोटक सामग्री विभिन्न स्थानमा फैलाउन सक्छ। यसका कारण एकैपटक ठूलो क्षेत्र प्रभावित हुन सक्ने भएकाले यस्ता हतियारको प्रयोगलाई लिएर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरमा गम्भीर मानवीय तथा सुरक्षा चिन्ता रहँदै आएको छ।

पछिल्लो परीक्षणको निरीक्षण उत्तर कोरियाको सत्तारूढ वर्कर्स पार्टीको केन्द्रीय सैन्य आयोगका सदस्य जनरल किम जोङ-सिकले गरेको समाचारमा उल्लेख छ। तर उत्तर कोरियाली नेता किम जोङ-उन स्वयं परीक्षणस्थलमा उपस्थित थिए भन्ने जानकारी सार्वजनिक गरिएको छैन।

उत्तर कोरियाले यसअघि अक्टोबर ३१ मा पनि रणनीतिकभन्दा फरक प्रकारको ब्यालिस्टिक मिसाइलमा प्रयोग गर्न सकिने क्लस्टर वारहेड परीक्षण गरेको थियो। उक्त परीक्षणमा १२ देखि १३ हेक्टरसम्मको क्षेत्र प्रभावित पार्न सक्ने दाबी गरिएको थियो।

लगातार भइरहेका यी परीक्षणलाई उत्तर कोरियाले आफ्नो रक्षा क्षमता सुदृढ गर्ने प्रयासका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेको छ। उत्तर कोरियाली अधिकारीहरूले बाह्य सुरक्षा चुनौतीहरूको सामना गर्न आधुनिक हतियार प्रणालीको विकास आवश्यक रहेको बताएका छन्।

उत्तर कोरियाले सन् २०२६ को अन्त्यसम्म विभिन्न प्रकारका क्लस्टर वारहेड सैन्य प्रयोगका लागि उपलब्ध गराउने लक्ष्यसमेत सार्वजनिक गरेको छ।

यसैबीच, उत्तर कोरियाको लगातारको मिसाइल परीक्षणले कोरियाली प्रायद्वीपको सुरक्षा अवस्थाबारे नयाँ चिन्ता उत्पन्न गरेको छ। दक्षिण कोरिया र अमेरिकाले उत्तर कोरियाको सैन्य गतिविधिलाई नजिकबाट निगरानी गर्दै आएका छन्।

A deadly helicopter accident occurred in Nepal’s Khumbu region of Solukhumbu district on Tuesday morning after two helicopters belonging to Fishtail Air and Dynasty Air collided mid-air. The accident took place at around 8:11 AM in Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality-4, killing one Indian tourist and injuring three others.

According to Solukhumbu police, the deceased has been identified as Indian national Vasant Kumar Balaramaramadu, who was travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter. His body was taken to a hospital in Lukla.

Another passenger, Shailesh Krishna Patel, a New Zealand citizen of Indian origin, was injured and airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu for treatment. Both helicopters' pilots also sustained minor injuries and were brought to Kathmandu for further medical care.

Authorities have yet to disclose what caused the two helicopters to collide. Further details about the accident are awaited.

नेपाल सरकारले सडक निर्माणमा नयाँ नीति अघि सारेको छ। प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह (बालेन) नेतृत्वको सरकारले विदेशबाट आयात गरिने बिटुमिन अर्थात् अलकत्राको विकल्पमा नेपालमै उत्पादित सिमेन्ट प्रयोग गरेर सडक निर्माण गर्ने योजनालाई प्राथमिकता दिएको हो।

सरकारले ‘सार्वजनिक खरिदमा स्वदेशी उत्पादनको प्रवर्द्धन र प्रयोगसम्बन्धी निर्देशिका, २०८३’ स्वीकृत गरेसँगै सडक निर्माणमा स्वदेशी सिमेन्टको प्रयोग बढाउने बाटो खुलेको छ। यस निर्णयले नेपालका सिमेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्नुका साथै विदेशबाट आयात हुने निर्माण सामग्रीमाथिको निर्भरता घटाउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्रालयका अनुसार अब सडक निर्माण गर्नुअघि कुन स्थानमा कालोपत्रे गर्ने र कुन स्थानमा सिमेन्ट प्रयोग गरेर कंक्रिट ढलान गर्ने भन्ने विषय प्राविधिक अध्ययनका आधारमा निर्धारण गरिनेछ।

विशेषगरी पहाडी क्षेत्रका उकालो, घुमाउरो सडक, ओसिलो स्थान तथा कालोपत्रे छिट्टै बिग्रिने क्षेत्रमा सिमेन्टबाट सडक निर्माणलाई प्राथमिकता दिइने भएको छ। त्यस्ता स्थानमा कंक्रिट सडक बढी टिकाउ हुन सक्ने सरकारी अधिकारीहरूको भनाइ छ।

यसअघि नेपालमा अधिकांश सडक निर्माणका लागि विदेशबाट आयात गरिएको बिटुमिन प्रयोग गरिँदै आएको थियो। तर अब सरकारले स्वदेशमै उपलब्ध गुणस्तरीय सिमेन्ट तथा अन्य निर्माण सामग्री प्रयोग बढाउने नीति लिएको छ।

सरकारको नयाँ व्यवस्थाअनुसार सडक, पुल तथा सरकारी भवनका आयोजना डिजाइन गर्दादेखि नै उपयुक्त स्वदेशी सामग्रीलाई प्राथमिकता दिनुपर्नेछ। बोलपत्र तथा निर्माण सम्झौतामा समेत स्वदेशी सामग्री प्रयोगसम्बन्धी व्यवस्था समावेश गरिनेछ।

सिमेन्ट सडक निर्माणमा कति खर्च लाग्छ?

नेपाल निर्माण व्यवसायी महासंघले उपलब्ध गराएको लागत विवरणअनुसार साढे पाँच मिटर चौडाइको एक किलोमिटर अस्फाल्ट कालोपत्रे सडक निर्माण गर्न करिब १ करोड ७७ लाख रुपैयाँ लाग्छ। सोही आकारको सिमेन्ट कंक्रिट सडक निर्माण गर्दा करिब ३ करोड ५ लाख रुपैयाँ खर्च हुने अनुमान छ।

सिमेन्ट सडकको सुरुवाती निर्माण लागत बढी भए पनि लामो समय टिक्न सक्ने र मर्मतमा लाग्ने खर्च घट्न सक्ने भएकाले यसको प्रयोग बढाउनुपर्ने निर्माण व्यवसायीहरूको भनाइ छ।

यद्यपि, सरकारले देशभरका सबै सडक एकैपटक सिमेन्टबाट बनाउने निर्णय भने गरेको छैन। प्राविधिक रूपमा उपयुक्त र आवश्यक देखिएका स्थानमा मात्रै सिमेन्ट कंक्रिट सडक निर्माण गरिनेछ।

सरकारले सिमेन्ट सडक निर्माणका लागि छुट्टै बोलपत्र आह्वान गर्ने तयारीसमेत अघि बढाएको छ। निर्माण अघि नै प्राविधिक अध्ययन गरेर कुन सडकमा कुन सामग्री उपयुक्त हुन्छ भन्ने निर्धारण गरिनेछ।

सरकारले देशभर एउटै ब्रान्डको एलपी ग्यास सिलिन्डर लागू गर्ने तयारी थालेको छ। बजारमा विभिन्न कम्पनीका सिलिन्डर प्रयोग भइरहँदा उपभोक्ताले ग्यास सकिएपछि अर्को ब्रान्डको सिलिन्डरसँग साट्न समस्या भोग्दै आएका छन्। यही समस्या समाधान गर्ने उद्देश्यले सरकारले एउटै ब्रान्डको सिलिन्डर प्रणाली लागू गर्ने तयारी अघि बढाएको हो।

विशेषगरी एउटा कम्पनीको ग्यास प्रयोग गर्ने उपभोक्ताले अर्को कम्पनीको ग्यास पसलबाट सिलिन्डर साट्न नपाउँदा खाली सिलिन्डर बोकेर सम्बन्धित कम्पनीको डिलर खोज्नुपर्ने बाध्यता छ। एउटै ब्रान्ड लागू भएमा यस्तो समस्या हट्ने र ग्यास वितरण तथा आपूर्तिमा सहजता आउने सरकारको अपेक्षा छ।

यद्यपि, एउटै ब्रान्डको सिलिन्डर लागू गर्ने योजना कसरी कार्यान्वयन गर्ने, हाल बजारमा रहेका ५८ ब्रान्डका सिलिन्डरको व्यवस्थापन कसरी गर्ने र ग्यास उद्योगहरूलाई कसरी समेट्ने भन्ने विषयमा थप तयारी आवश्यक हुनेछ। सरकारले यस योजनालाई कार्यान्वयनमा ल्याउन सके एलपी ग्यास प्रयोग गर्ने देशभरका उपभोक्तालाई प्रत्यक्ष राहत पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

इरानको केश्म टापुमा अमेरिकाको सैन्य हमला! विस्फोटपछि मध्यपूर्वमा फेरि तनाव बढ्ने चिन्ता!

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सञ्चारमाध्यमका रिपोर्टअनुसार नोभेम्बर २ मा अमेरिकी सेनाले केश्म टापुलाई लक्षित गरी सैन्य कारबाही गरेको हो। अमेरिकी अधिकारीहरूले इरानी पक्षबाट अमेरिकी विमानमाथि खतरा उत्पन्न भएपछि आत्मरक्षाका लागि जवाफी कदम चालिएको दाबी गरेका छन्।

इरानी सरकारी सञ्चारमाध्यमले पनि टापुमा विस्फोटका आवाज सुनिएको जनाएका छन्। यद्यपि, हमलाबाट भएको वास्तविक क्षति, लक्षित सैन्य संरचना तथा मानवीय हताहतीको पूर्ण विवरण सार्वजनिक भएको छैन।

केश्म टापु किन महत्त्वपूर्ण छ?

केश्म टापु इरानको दक्षिणी क्षेत्रमा, विश्वकै प्रमुख तेल ढुवानी मार्ग होर्मुज जलडमरूमध्यनजिक अवस्थित छ। यो क्षेत्रबाट ठूलो मात्रामा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय तेल तथा ऊर्जा सामग्री ढुवानी हुने भएकाले यहाँ हुने सैन्य गतिविधिले विश्व ऊर्जा बजारमा समेत प्रभाव पार्न सक्छ।

पछिल्लो घटनापछि मध्यपूर्वको सुरक्षा अवस्था र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय तेल आपूर्तिबारे चिन्ता बढेको छ। तनाव थप चर्किए तेलको मूल्य तथा विश्व व्यापारमा असर पर्न सक्ने विश्लेषण गरिएको छ।

अमेरिकी अधिकारीहरूले भने यो कारबाहीलाई ठूलो युद्धको सुरुवात नभई सीमित तथा रक्षात्मक कदमका रूपमा व्याख्या गरेका छन्।

अमेरिका र इरानबीचको तनाव समाधानका लागि कूटनीतिक प्रयास भइरहे पनि सैन्य गतिविधिले वार्ताको वातावरण थप जटिल बनाउने चिन्ता व्यक्त गरिएको छ।

इरानको केश्म टापुमा भएको पछिल्लो घटनाले मध्यपूर्वको तनाव अझै कम नभएको संकेत गरेको छ। अब राष्ट्रपति ट्रम्पले वार्तालाई प्राथमिकता दिन्छन् वा इरानमाथि थप सैन्य दबाब बढाउँछन् भन्ने विषयमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय समुदायको ध्यान केन्द्रित भएको छ।

किसानले उत्पादन गरेको दूधको भुक्तानी कर्मचारीका व्यक्तिगत खातामा जम्मा गरेर दुग्ध विकास संस्थान (डिडिसी) मा १२ करोड रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी घोटाला गरेको खुलेको छ । नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरो (सिआइबी) ले गरेको अनुसन्धानमा तत्कालीन महाप्रबन्धक सञ्जीव झासहित कर्मचारीहरूको मिलेमतोमा रकम हिनामिना भएको देखिएको हो ।

गत जेठ ७ गते परेको उजुरीका आधारमा अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको सिआइबीले लैनचौरस्थित डिडिसीको केन्द्रीय कार्यालय र बालाजुस्थित काठमाडौं दुग्ध कार्यालयमा छापा मारेर कागजात नियन्त्रणमा लिएको थियो । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा १७ वटा कृषि तथा पशुपालन फार्म र सहकारीमार्फत कर्मचारीका खातामा रकम गएको खुलेको छ ।

कर्मचारीहरूले किसानलाई दूधमा रहेको चिल्लो पदार्थ र एसएनएफको वास्तविक विवरण नदिई बढी भुक्तानी देखाउने र त्यसको केही रकम आफ्नो खातामा फिर्ता लिन लगाउने गरेको अनुसन्धानमा खुलेको छ । कतिपय अवस्थामा किसानले पठाएको दूधमा समस्या आएको भन्दै अर्को फार्मको दूध थपेर परिमाण बढाउने र थप देखाइएको रकम कर्मचारीले लिने गरेको पाइएको छ ।

अनुसन्धानअनुसार लालीगुराँस पशुपालन फार्मबाट मात्रै कर्मचारीको खातामा चार करोड ४२ लाख रुपैयाँ आएको छ । दुर्घटनामा मृत्यु भएका रितेश राय यादवको खातामा विभिन्न कृषि फार्मबाट दुई करोड ७८ लाख रुपैयाँ जम्मा भएको देखिएको छ । त्यस्तै रामकेवल रायको खातामा एक करोड १४ लाख र उनका छोरा जितेन्द्रकुमार यादवको खातामा एक करोड ३२ लाख रुपैयाँ आएको सिआइबीको अनुसन्धानमा उल्लेख छ ।

यसैगरी, कर्मचारी मनहरि शर्माको खातामा एक करोड १५ लाख, शिवनन्द रायको खातामा एक करोड ६९ लाख र नवीन राय यादवले एक करोड ९३ लाख रुपैयाँ लिएको अनुसन्धानबाट खुलेको छ । तत्कालीन महाप्रबन्धक झाको कार्यकालमा मात्रै पाँच करोड रुपैयाँ घोटाला भएको सिआइबीको दाबी छ ।

यस प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन महाप्रबन्धक झासहित आठ जना पक्राउ परिसकेका छन् । केही अन्य व्यक्ति फरार रहेको र उनीहरूको खोजी भइरहेको सिआइबीले जनाएको छ । पक्राउ परेकाहरूमाथि आपराधिक विश्वासघात र संगठित अपराधसम्बन्धी कसुरमा अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ । अदालतले उनीहरूलाई सात दिन हिरासतमा राख्न अनुमति दिएको छ ।

सिआइबीका प्रमुख एआईजी उमाप्रसाद चतुर्वेदीले किसानको रकम नेतृत्वदेखि तल्लो तहका कर्मचारीसम्मको मिलेमतोमा हिनामिना भएको अनुसन्धानबाट खुलेको बताएका छन् ।

बलिउडका सुपरस्टार शाहरुख खान फेरि भारतकै सबैभन्दा धनी अभिनेताको सूचीमा पहिलो स्थानमा परेका छन्। चलचित्र अभिनयसँगै व्यापार, विज्ञापन, फिल्म निर्माण र क्रिकेटमा लगानी गर्दै आएका शाहरुखको कुल सम्पत्ति करिब १० हजार करोड भारतीय रुपैयाँ पुगेको छ।

हालै सार्वजनिक भएको ‘हुरुन इन्डिया रिच लिस्ट २०२६’ अनुसार शाहरुख खान भारतका अन्य चर्चित अभिनेता अमिताभ बच्चन, सलमान खान र ऋतिक रोशनलाई पछि पार्दै सबैभन्दा धनी अभिनेता बनेका हुन्।

शाहरुखले चलचित्रबाट मात्रै नभई विभिन्न व्यावसायिक क्षेत्रमा गरेको लगानीबाट पनि ठूलो सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेका छन्। उनको फिल्म निर्माण कम्पनी **रेड चिलीज इन्टरटेनमेन्ट र क्रिकेट फ्रेन्चाइजसँग सम्बन्धित नाइट राइडर्स स्पोर्ट्स उनका प्रमुख व्यावसायिक सम्पत्तिमध्ये पर्छन्।

यसैगरी विभिन्न अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय ब्रान्डका विज्ञापन, व्यापारिक साझेदारी तथा घरजग्गामा गरिएको लगानीले पनि उनको आर्थिक साम्राज्य विस्तार भएको छ।

शाहरुख खानको सम्पत्तिसँगै मुम्बईको बान्द्रामा रहेको उनको प्रसिद्ध घर ‘मन्नत’ पनि चर्चामा आएको छ।

मन्नत शाहरुखको निजी निवास मात्रै नभई उनका प्रशंसकहरूका लागि आकर्षणको केन्द्रसमेत बनेको छ। उनको जन्मदिन तथा विशेष अवसरहरूमा घरबाहिर ठूलो संख्यामा प्रशंसक भेला हुने गर्छन्।

सार्वजनिक विवरणअनुसार अमिताभ बच्चन करिब ४ हजार करोड रुपैयाँसहित दोस्रो स्थानमा छन्। सलमान खानको सम्पत्ति करिब ३ हजार करोड र ऋतिक रोशनको करिब २ हजार ५०० करोड रुपैयाँ अनुमान गरिएको छ।

१,९९९ अमेरिकी डलरबाट मूल्य सुरु हुने यो फोन खोल्दा ठूलो स्क्रिनमा प्रयोग गर्न सकिन्छ। नयाँ डिजाइन, शक्तिशाली प्रोसेसर र मल्टिटास्किङ सुविधाका कारण फोल्डेबल आइफोनलाई एप्पलको महत्त्वपूर्ण उत्पादन मानिएको छ।

यस कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत विश्वभरबाट १६ जना अविवाहित व्यक्ति छनोट गरिनेछन्। छनोट भएका सहभागीले चार दिनसम्म फिनल्यान्ड घुम्ने, स्थानीय खानपानको अनुभव गर्ने र त्यहाँका अविवाहित व्यक्तिहरूसँग सामूहिक डिनर डेटमा सहभागी हुने अवसर पाउनेछन्।

जापानका लागि प्रस्तावित नेपाली राजदूत जिज्ञानकुमार थापाले नाम फिर्ता लिए

यसअघि जापानको स्थायी बसोबास अनुमति (पीआर) त्यागेको विषय र नेपालको संविधानको धारा २९१ अनुसार उनको योग्यतामाथि प्रश्न उठेपछि सुनुवाइ प्रक्रिया रोकिएको थियो।

थापाले आफूले जापानको पीआर त्यागिसकेको स्पष्टीकरण दिएका थिए। तर, सांसदहरूले पीआर त्यागेको समय र जापानसँगको उनको सम्बन्धबारे थप प्रश्न उठाएका थिए।

इरानका सर्वोच्च नेता आयातोल्लाह अली खामेनीको मृत्यु र त्यसपछि इरानी नेतृत्वमा भएको ठूलो क्षतिबारे अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्पले दिएको टिप्पणीले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय राजनीतिमा नयाँ चर्चा सुरु भएको छ। इरानका शीर्ष नेताहरू मारिएपछि अब वार्ता गर्ने व्यक्ति पहिचान गर्नसमेत कठिन भएको भन्दै ट्रम्पले अमेरिकी सैन्य कारबाही आवश्यकताभन्दा बढी अगाडि गएको हुन सक्ने बताएका छन्।

गत फेब्रुअरी २८ मा अमेरिका र इजरायलले इरानमाथि संयुक्त सैन्य कारबाही सुरु गरेका थिए। त्यसक्रममा इरानका तत्कालीन सर्वोच्च नेता आयातोल्लाह अली खामेनीसहित उच्च राजनीतिक तथा सैन्य अधिकारीहरूको मृत्यु भएको थियो।

खामेनीको मृत्युपछि इरानको सर्वोच्च नेतृत्वमा उनका छोरा मोज्तबा खामेनी आएका छन्। तर इरानको वास्तविक निर्णय प्रक्रिया र वार्ताका लागि जिम्मेवार अधिकारीहरूबारे अमेरिकी प्रशासनले पटकपटक अन्योल व्यक्त गर्दै आएको छ।

यसैबीच, अक्टोबर १२ मा अमेरिकाको ओहायो राज्यमा आयोजित चुनावी सभालाई सम्बोधन गर्दै राष्ट्रपति ट्रम्पले इरानको नेतृत्व तहमा गरिएको कारबाहीबारे अनौठो टिप्पणी गरेका थिए।

ट्रम्पले इरानी नेताहरूविरुद्धको कारबाहीमा अमेरिका आवश्यकताभन्दा बढी अगाडि गएको हुन सक्ने बताएका थिए। उनका अनुसार नेतृत्व तहमा लगातार परिवर्तन हुँदा अब वासिङ्टनले वार्ता गर्नुपर्ने व्यक्तिको पहिचान गर्न कठिन भइरहेको छ।

ट्रम्पले इरानका धेरै वरिष्ठ नेताहरू मारिएको दाबी गर्दै त्यसपछि जिम्मेवारी सम्हाल्ने अधिकारीहरूसमेत प्रभावित भएकाले वार्ताको वातावरण जटिल बनेको उल्लेख गरेका थिए।

उनको यो भनाइलाई लिएर अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सञ्चारमाध्यममा अमेरिकी रणनीतिमाथि प्रश्न उठेको छ। सैन्य दबाबमार्फत इरानलाई वार्तामा ल्याउने प्रयास गरिए पनि नेतृत्व संरचनामा आएको परिवर्तनले कूटनीतिक प्रक्रिया थप जटिल बनाउन सक्ने चर्चा सुरु भएको छ।

अक्टोबर १४ मा एरिजोनामा आयोजित अर्को कार्यक्रममा पनि ट्रम्पले यस्तै आशयको टिप्पणी दोहोर्‍याएका थिए। उनले इरानसँग कसलाई सम्पर्क गर्ने भन्ने विषय स्पष्ट नभएको बताएका थिए।

चलचित्र विकास बोर्डले सार्वजनिक गरेको पछिल्लो आधिकारिक बक्स अफिस विवरणअनुसार ‘कबड्डी ५’ ले प्रदर्शनको १० दिनमा १० करोड ७६ लाख ७३ हजार ७१५ रुपैयाँ ग्रस कलेक्सन गरेको छ। यस अवधिमा चलचित्रका ३ लाख ४६ हजार ४२७ टिकट बिक्री भएका छन्।

‘१२ गाउँ २’ असोज ३० गतेदेखि प्रदर्शनमा आएको थियो भने ‘कबड्डी ५’ कात्तिक ६ गतेदेखि प्रदर्शनमा आएको हो। पछि प्रदर्शनमा आए पनि ‘कबड्डी ५’ ले टिकट बिक्री र कुल कमाइ दुवैमा बलियो अग्रता लिएको छ।

रामबाबु गुरुङको निर्देशनमा बनेको ‘कबड्डी ५’ मा दयाहाङ राईसँगै विपिन कार्की, विजय बराल, बुद्धि तामाङ, मिरुना मगर, रिश्मा गुरुङलगायतका कलाकारको अभिनय रहेको छ।

कबड्डी सिरिज यसअघि नै दर्शकमाझ लोकप्रिय भइसकेको चलचित्र शृंखला हो। ग्रामीण परिवेश, प्रेम, हास्य र सामाजिक सम्बन्धमा आधारित कथाले दर्शकको ध्यान तान्दै आएको छ। पाँचौँ शृंखलाले समेत बक्स अफिसमा राम्रो व्यापार गर्न सफल भएको छ।

यसैबीच, विराज भट्टको निर्देशनमा तयार भएको ‘१२ गाउँ २’ मा उनका छोरा समीर भट्ट प्रमुख भूमिकामा छन्। एक्सनप्रधान प्रस्तुतिका कारण चर्चामा रहेको चलचित्रले अपेक्षाकृत कम व्यापार गरेको देखिएको छ।

‘१२ गाउँ’ को पहिलो शृंखलाले व्यावसायिक सफलता हासिल गरेपछि दोस्रो भागप्रति पनि दर्शकको चासो थियो। तर पछिल्लो सार्वजनिक तथ्यांकले सिक्वेल चलचित्रको सफलता पहिलो भागको लोकप्रियतामा मात्रै निर्भर नहुने संकेत गरेको छ।

वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा जान चाहने नेपालीहरूका लागि अर्को अवसरको ढोका खुल्ने भएको छ। अफ्रिकानजिकै हिन्द महासागरमा अवस्थित टापु राष्ट्र मौरिससले नेपालबाट सरकारी संयन्त्रमार्फत श्रमिक लैजाने प्रस्तावमा सहमति जनाएको छ।

Thousands of Strangers Become Family at Chinese Groom’s Wedding

A 24-year-old Chinese man who feared his wedding would be almost empty ended up celebrating with thousands of strangers after a heartfelt social media invitation went viral.

Xu Chenghong, who lost his father at age three and his grandmother at seven, grew up with very few close family members. After years of hard work, he finally saved enough to marry his girlfriend, but feared that only a handful of guests would attend.

Hoping to make the day less lonely, he posted an invitation on Douyin, China's version of TikTok, asking strangers to join his wedding. He expected around 10 to 20 people to show up.

Instead, thousands of people reportedly travelled from across China to celebrate with the couple. Some brought livestock, food and household appliances, while volunteer chefs prepared meals and supporters helped organise the event. A Maybach was even arranged for the newlyweds.

The overwhelming response forced organisers to move the celebration to a larger venue, with local authorities helping manage the crowds.

What began as a simple request for a few wedding guests became an extraordinary celebration of kindness, proving that family is not always defined by blood, but by the people who show up when it matters most.

Too Much Screen Time in Schools? Sweden Is Changing Its Education Strategy

Sweden is rethinking its technology-driven education strategy after growing concerns about the impact of excessive screen use on children's learning. Once among the countries enthusiastically introducing laptops and tablets into classrooms, Sweden is now shifting its focus back towards printed textbooks, handwriting and traditional reading.

The change follows concerns over declining reading performance among fourth-grade students between 2016 and 2021. Educators and researchers have raised questions about children's concentration, reading comprehension and dependence on digital devices. In response, Sweden has invested more than 2.1 billion Swedish kronor in printed textbooks and teacher guides.

The country has also changed its approach to early childhood education, with preschools no longer required to use digital tools. More classroom time is being directed towards reading physical books and practising handwriting, while a nationwide mobile phone ban in schools is planned.

However, Sweden's shift does not mean completely rejecting technology. Digital skills remain important for children's future, but policymakers are increasingly recognising that screens are not necessarily the best learning tool for every age group or subject. The country's experience highlights an important lesson for education systems worldwide: technological innovation should support learning, not replace the fundamentals of reading, writing and focused attention.

The real story: Two female belugas with marked spinal deformities washed ashore on the banks of the St. Lawrence River in Quebec and were examined at the Université de Montréal's Faculty of Veterinary Medicine with CT scans. Both were emaciated. In the first, a 17-year-old female, arthritis caused by the deformities likely contributed to her death. Source: Canadian Wildlife Health Cooperative (CWHC-Quebec), published 2026.

Researchers who watch St. Lawrence belugas from boats had seen it before: now and then, a living whale with a visibly bent spine. What nobody had done was examine one up close. Then two female belugas with marked spinal deformities washed ashore on the banks of the river, and the Quebec team of the Canadian Wildlife Health Cooperative finally had the chance.

Both whales were taken to the Université de Montréal's Faculty of Veterinary Medicine for post-mortem examination and computed tomography scans. Both were emaciated. In the first, a 17-year-old young adult female, the scientists found significant degenerative osteoarthritis secondary to the spinal deformities. They concluded that these bone malformations ultimately contributed to her death, most likely by making it harder for her to move and feed.

The finding is both small and large. A preliminary review of photographs of living belugas collected since 2003 by the Group for Research and Education on Marine Mammals suggests that vertebral deformities are present in fewer than 3 percent of the whales photographed. What causes them is still not known; the researchers say the two examinations "pave the way" for further investigation. For a population already struggling to raise calves, every animal that can't hunt properly is another loss, and a question still waiting for an answer.

TRAPPED INSIDE A 1,000-DEGREE INFERNO FOR 90 SECONDS. In March 2001, Phoenix Police Officer Jason Schechterle was stopped at a red light in his Crown Victoria cruiser when a vehicle traveling over 115 mph rear-ended him, rupturing the fuel tank and igniting a blinding fireball. Trapped inside with crumpled doors, he survived fourth-degree burns across 40% of his body, endured over 50 surgeries, and built an unbreakable life out of the ashes.

“I was trapped in a cage of fire for a minute and a half. When I finally woke up from a two-and-a-half-month coma, my face was gone, my hands were severely damaged, and my life as I knew it had vanished. But tragedy doesn't define who you are—your response to it does. There is nothing in this world as powerful as a made-up mind.”

— Officer Jason Schechterle, Phoenix Police Department & Author of Burning Shield

The Incident & The 90-Second Rescue
The 115 MPH Collision: Stopped at an intersection on Thomas Road in Phoenix, Arizona, Officer Jason Schechterle’s patrol vehicle was rear-ended at highway speeds by a driver who had suffered a medical seizure behind the wheel.

 The severe impact crushed the Crown Victoria’s rear crumple zone into the fuel tank, sparking an immediate 1,000-degree gasoline fire that engulfed the passenger cabin and jammed the doors shut.

Phoenix Fire Captain Gary West was nearby when the crash occurred. Armed with only a small dry-chemical extinguisher, he fought through intense heat, forced open the mangled door frame, and pulled Schechterle from the burning cockpit with seconds to spare.

 Schechterle sustained devastating fourth-degree burns across more than 40% of his body, losing his ears, nose, eyelids, and facial skin. Placed into a medically induced coma for two and a half months, he underwent more than 50 surgeries to reconstruct his features and restore eyesight.

Demonstrating extraordinary resilience, Schechterle returned to work with the Phoenix Police Department, authored his autobiography Burning Shield, and became an internationally renowned keynote speaker on overcoming life-altering adversity.

Key Lessons on Resilience & Overcoming Adversity
Focusing on the Response, Not the Circumstance: Pain and trauma are inevitable, but victimhood is a choice. Reframing catastrophic injury into a platform for service enables long-term psychological recovery.

Winning the Internal Battle: Recovery from severe physical trauma is primarily cognitive. Rebuilding daily discipline and maintaining positive internal dialogue prevents despair from taking root.

The Power of First Responder Brotherhood: Schechterle’s survival was made possible by the decisive, selfless courage of a firefighter who entered a raging vehicle fire without full protective gear to save a brother officer.

It's one of the most improbable images in the history of air combat: one fighter jet, over enemy territory, physically pushing another crippled jet through the sky to keep it flying. It really happened, on March 10, 1967, over North Vietnam, and it's remembered as Pardo's Push.

During a strike near Hanoi, two F-4 Phantoms were hit by anti-aircraft fire. Captain Earl Aman's jet took the worst of it, his fuel tank holed, draining fast, with no tanker in reach. He and his backseater were about to go down deep in enemy territory. His wingman, Captain Bob Pardo, refused to let that happen.

Pardo had Aman lower his tailhook, the steel hook used to catch wires on a carrier, then eased it against the glass of his own windshield and began to push. Aman shut down his engines. For about 20 minutes, one Phantom flew two, the hook slipping off every few seconds, Pardo repositioning and pushing again, until he'd driven the dying jet some 80 miles into Laos. Then his own engine caught fire and he ejected too.

All four men were rescued within two hours. Pardo's reward at first was a reprimand for risking the aircraft. It took 22 years before he got the Silver Star. He never called it heroism, he just refused to leave his wingman behind.

“EVIDENCE INDICATES PARTS OF THE JET BROKE OFF BEFORE IMPACT.” — Federal investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board reveal that the doomed Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, likely suffered an in-flight structural breakup at altitude, aligning with dashcam video appearing to show the aircraft plunging nose-first without its T-tail horizontal stabilizer.

“There are indications the aircraft began breaking up prior to impact. We may find parts of the aircraft some distance away from the actual impact site... We are asking anyone in the community who locates debris to contact local law enforcement immediately.”

— National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) Press Briefing in Palm Beach County

“We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence... Mayday, mayday, we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute... We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute... We’re going to crash into the ground.”

— Cockpit transmissions broadcast over Air Traffic Control frequencies moments before impact

Aerodynamic & Forensic Breakdown
The In-Flight Breakup Finding: During their initial media briefing in Palm Beach County, NTSB investigators confirmed that the Learjet 60 began shedding components prior to striking the ground, officially expanding the search radius across residential neighborhoods miles away from the primary impact crater.

The Missing Horizontal Stabilizer: Close-up frame analysis of civilian dashcam footage captured seconds before impact appears to show the aircraft's T-tail fuselage cleanly sheared off, missing the entire horizontal stabilizer and elevator assembly that controls aircraft pitch.

Why Loss of the Stabilizer is Fatal: On swept-wing, T-tail jets like the Learjet 60, the horizontal stabilizer generates continuous downward aerodynamic force to counter the natural forward center of gravity. If the stabilizer separates due to severe structural flutter, pitch trim runaway, or aerodynamic over-stress, the aircraft immediately lawn-darts into a near-vertical terminal dive that is physically impossible to pull out of, regardless of pilot yoke input.

The Escalating Mayday Telemetry: Flight tracking telemetry and ATC recordings show the crew encountered severe weather and icing while climbing through 8,700 feet. The aircraft suddenly entered an uncontrollable overspeed condition, with vertical descent rates accelerating from 10,000 FPM past 32,000 FPM before the violent ground collision.

Key Investigation Priorities for the NTSB
Locating the Empennage Components: Ground teams are prioritizing the recovery of tail structure fragments, elevator control horns, and pitch trim actuators to determine whether failure was aerodynamic, mechanical, or structural.

Analyzing Trim Jackscrew Position: Recovery crews will inspect the horizontal stabilizer trim actuator jackscrew to determine if an uncommanded runaway pitch condition preceded the structural separation.

Evaluating Atmospheric Stress & Icing: Meteorologists and investigators are analyzing weather radar data to evaluate whether severe convective turbulence or structural ice accumulation induced catastrophic aerodynamic loading at cruise altitude.

When the Civil War broke out, Mary Walker wasn't asking for permission. She was already a doctor, one of the very few women in America who could say that back in 1855. The Army told her women couldn't serve as surgeons. So she showed up anyway and worked for free.

She treated wounded Union soldiers in field hospitals, often close to the fighting. She'd cross into dangerous ground to care for civilians too, and in April 1864 that cost her. Confederate troops captured her and accused her of being a spy. She spent four months locked up in Castle Thunder prison in Richmond before she was traded back in a prisoner exchange.

In November 1865, President Andrew Johnson awarded her the Medal of Honor.

But her story didn't end neatly. In 1917, the government tightened the rules and took the medal back from her and hundreds of others. Mary's answer? She refused to return it. She wore it every single day until she died in 1919.

It took almost 60 more years, but in 1977 President Jimmy Carter restored her medal.

To this day, she is the only woman ever to receive the Medal of Honor.

She was stubborn, fearless, and way ahead of her time. And she never once backed down.

Rest easy, Dr. Walker. 🇺🇸

Prisoners of war have tried everything to escape, but few plans were as patient — or as strange — as Benjamin Purcell's. Held in a North Vietnamese prison camp, the Army officer spent months secretly drilling tiny holes into his cell door, a little at a time, always watching for the guards. His early-warning system was a chicken he had trained to react whenever anyone approached.

He would not see freedom until 1973. He retired as a colonel, carrying one of the most remarkable escape stories of the Vietnam War: no tools, no help, just patience, nerve, and a chicken.

Compounding the Recruiting Crisis: As all branches battle historically challenging recruiting environments, losing experienced mid-career NCOs and junior officers over political fatigue threatens institutional knowledge, unit cohesion, and technical combat capabilities.

Erosion of Public Trust: Decades of defense polling demonstrate that public confidence in the armed forces relies directly on its strictly non-partisan status. Partisan debates over command appointments, social messaging, and foreign policy rhetoric risk undermining that foundational trust.

Mission Focus vs. Narrative Battles: Frontline leaders emphasize that unit effectiveness hinges on warfighting competency, tactical drills, and equipment readiness, warning that culture-war distractions degrade morale in operational formations.

Honoring the memory and heroism of U.S. Marine Corporal Seamus M. Davey, an elite reconnaissance scout with 2d Force Reconnaissance Company (attached to 4th Force Recon Battalion).

On October 21, 2005, during combat operations in Abu Hyatt, Al Anbar Province, Iraq, Cpl. Davey's team entered an insurgent staging house and was ambushed at point-blank range—less than ten feet away—by four armed enemy fighters.

Struck by multiple rounds, Davey collapsed to the ground. Completely disregarding his mortal wounds and personal safety, he immediately brought his weapon to bear and opened continuous suppressive fire on the gunmen. His decisive, selfless actions drew the enemy's fire away from the doorway, allowing his fellow Marines to safely withdraw from the kill zone and survive. Davey continued to engage the enemy until he succumbed to his wounds, just three days before his 26th birthday.

For his extraordinary heroism, he was posthumously awarded the Bronze Star Medal with Combat "V" and the Purple Heart.

"Swift, Silent, Deadly." Semper Fidelis, Corporal Davey. Your brothers will never forget.

The Polish Armed Forces have officially received their first operational shipment of South Korean CTM-290 tactical ballistic missiles, boasting a precision strike range of 290 kilometers (approximately 180 miles).

The heavy deep-strike missiles are integrated into Poland's HOMAR-K rocket artillery system, which pairs the K239 multi-caliber launcher with a domestically manufactured Polish Jelcz 8×8 heavy armored chassis and Poland's proprietary TOPAZ automated fire control network. The newly arrived ballistic missiles dramatically expand Warsaw's long-range deterrence across the Suwałki Gap and along NATO's eastern flank.

One of the biggest questions hanging over the Western alliance isn't about any single battle or weapon. It's this: what happens to Europe if the United States steps back?

A new study from the RAND Corporation, the nonpartisan research institution, takes it head-on. Titled "Anticipating Allies' Responses to U.S. Retrenchment from Europe" and published October 28, 2026, it asks how America's four most important European allies, France, Germany, Poland, and the UK, would respond if Washington reduces its role, something the report notes the current administration has already begun in early steps.

The central finding is striking: the manner of any pullback matters most. A gradual, coordinated, well-communicated drawdown would likely keep allies aligned and still spending on defense. A sudden or unpredictable one could send them racing to cut their dependence on US weapons.

One reassuring note: RAND found little reason to think a US pullback would push these allies toward Russia or China. All four still see Russia as a threat. It helps explain why countries like Poland are building up their own forces so fast, hedging against exactly this uncertainty.

The takeaway: the question may be less whether America steps back in Europe than how. Handled carefully, the study says, the alliance can bend without breaking.

A Finnish conscript during Exercise Mighty Hammer 26. Compared with conscripts in many other countries, he looks remarkably well equipped, especially with a magnified optic on his rifle and a high cut ballistic helmet. There's a simple reason for that. In Finland, conscripts and reservists aren't a side project. They are the army.

Outside a relatively small professional cadre of officers, NCOs, and specialists, nearly everyone in Finland's wartime force is a conscript or a reservist. So when Finland invests in modern equipment, it goes to the same people who would actually be called on to fight. Today's conscript is tomorrow's reservist, and he's expected to be ready.

Led by the Armoured Brigade, Mighty Hammer 26 runs from October 23 to November 3 at the Pohjankangas training area in Niinisalo, with about 2,000 participants and nearly 400 vehicles, including 120 tanks and armored vehicles. The focus is on preparing troops for the realities of the modern battlefield, from countering drones to protecting against air threats.

A small country with a long border and no illusions about its neighbor.

“10 TO 11 MONTHS AWAY FROM HOME IS THE NEW NORMAL.” Navy Leadership Warns Sailors Traditional 7-Month Deployments Are Years Away.

For decades, a typical U.S. Navy carrier strike group deployment lasted six to seven months. But amid relentless operational demands in the Middle East and a severe shipyard maintenance backlog, the Pentagon is delivering a hard truth to sailors and their families: prepare for 10-to-11-month tours at sea.

Why Carrier Tours Keep Getting Extended:

 Continuous combat operations in the Red Sea countering Houthi missile and drone swarms have forced strike groups including the USS Gerald R. Ford (326 days at sea) and the USS Abraham Lincoln (over 320 days) into historic, repeated deployment extensions.

 Prolonged separations put intense psychological strain on military families, fueling concerns over burnout, mental health, and reenlistment rates among junior enlisted personnel.

Fleet Forces Command leadership notes that until the Navy has enough ship capacity and cleared maintenance backlogs, extended 10-to-11-month deployments will remain an expectation rather than an exception.

Picture the fastest jet ever built sitting on the runway, dripping. Before every mission, the SR-71 Blackbird leaked fuel onto the concrete, puddles of it spreading beneath the plane while the ground crew worked, completely unbothered. It looked like something was badly wrong. Nothing was. The leaking was deliberate, and it's one of the most ingenious stories in aviation.

The reason is heat. The Blackbird cruised faster than 2,000 mph, and air friction alone heated its skin to hundreds of degrees. Metal expands when it's that hot, so Lockheed built the fuselage and fuel tanks with deliberate gaps, loose on the ground, sealing tight only once the plane heated and stretched several inches longer in flight. On the cold ground, those gaps sat open, and the fuel seeped out. So the Blackbird took off light, then refueled from a tanker once airborne and sealed.

The fuel itself was so hard to ignite you could reportedly drop a lit match in it and it would go out. And the ultimate irony: to survive Mach 3 heat, the plane was about 85% titanium, which the US couldn't supply, so the CIA secretly bought it from the Soviet Union, the very country the SR-71 was built to spy on.

Retired in the 1990s, never officially replaced. The puddle under its wings wasn't a flaw. It was the signature of genius.

A comprehensive new defense survey and non-profit report have highlighted an alarming rise in food insecurity across the armed forces, revealing that an increasing number of junior enlisted households are relying on food banks and charitable assistance to make ends meet.   

Persistent inflation, surging off-base housing costs, and basic allowance for housing (BAH) shortfalls have severely squeezed junior enlisted paychecks, leaving many young military families unable to keep pace with everyday grocery and utility expenses. 

While the military provides comprehensive base pay and healthcare, lower-ranking service members (grades E-1 to E-4) often find themselves falling into financial vulnerability, particularly those with dependents stationed in high-cost-of-living areas. 

Charitable organizations, base relief societies, and local food distribution programs continue to step in to bridge the gap, sparking urgent renewed calls across Washington and the Pentagon for higher baseline compensation and structural pay reform for junior troops.

Former 75th Ranger Regiment sniper Nicholas Irving, known as "The Reaper," with his custom SR-25 sniper rifle, "Dirty Diana." Irving served as a sniper with 3rd Battalion, 75th Ranger Regiment, and during a single deployment to Afghanistan in 2009, he was credited with 33 confirmed kills, one of the highest totals for a single deployment in special operations history.

The SR-25 was the rifle at the center of it all. A semi-automatic 7.62mm platform, it gave Ranger snipers the ability to engage multiple targets quickly at range, a critical advantage in the fast moving fights Rangers were known for. Irving named his "Dirty Diana," after the Michael Jackson song, and the rifle became almost as well known as the man behind it.

After leaving the Army, Irving told his story in his memoir, "The Reaper," and has spent the years since teaching marksmanship and sharing what he learned with a new generation of shooters.

Rangers lead the way.

Donald Trump issued a stark warning regarding Tehran’s nuclear ambitions, asserting that American military assets in the region possess the precision and speed to neutralize Iran’s remaining nuclear infrastructure in a matter of minutes.

With multiple U.S. carrier strike groups, stealth fighter squadrons, and standoff missile platforms positioned across the Persian Gulf, Red Sea, and Eastern Mediterranean, discussions surrounding military deterrence have reached a boiling point.

Overwhelming Standoff Capability: U.S. Central Command maintains continuous stealth bomber rotations, F-35 fighter coverage, and submarine-launched Tomahawk cruise missiles capable of striking fortified targets simultaneously with zero radar warning.

One of the Pentagon's senior generals has been removed from the Joint Staff amid an investigation into leaked classified information. Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, until recently the commander of the 101st Airborne Division, was relieved on October 28 as the Joint Staff's director of strategy, plans and policy, and the case has been referred to the Justice Department.

He started with the drive to heal his teammates—and ended up fighting at the absolute tip of the spear until his final breath.

Chief Special Warfare Operator (SEAL) Collin Trent Thomas, pictured downrange kitted up for high-threat direct-action raids across the Global War on Terror.

Enlisting in the U.S. Navy at age 19, Thomas initially completed training as a Hospital Corpsman before tackling the brutal crucible of BUD/S to earn his Trident. His relentless pursuit of excellence propelled him through the ranks, serving first with East Coast platoons at SEAL Team 4 and SEAL Team 2 before passing the grueling selection process for the Naval Special Warfare Development Group (DEVGRU / SEAL Team 6).

Operating in the shadows with DEVGRU's Silver Squadron, Thomas deployed repeatedly into the most contested hot zones in the world. He was the quintessential quiet professional: intensely capable, humble, and fiercely devoted to the men to his left and right.

On August 18, 2010, during a high-stakes night raid against an insurgent compound in eastern Afghanistan, Chief Thomas was fatally struck by enemy small-arms fire while leading from the front. He was 33 years old. His service was recognized with the Silver Star, the Bronze Star with Valor, and the Purple Heart.

A warrior who gave everything he had until there was nothing left to give.

Fair winds and following seas, Chief Thomas. The Only Easy Day Was Yesterday. 🇺🇸🔱⚡🦅

Cmdr. Brian Bourgeois, commanding officer of SEAL Team 8, died on December 7, 2021, three days after being injured in a fall during fast rope training from a helicopter near Virginia Beach. He was 43 years old.

Born and raised in Lake Charles, Louisiana, Bourgeois played four years of football as a safety at the U.S. Naval Academy before commissioning in 2001. After a brief tour on a ship, he earned his Trident and joined the Teams, going on to serve more than two decades in uniform. Among his awards was the Bronze Star with Valor. In November 2020, he took command of SEAL Team 8.

The leaders who served with him called him one of Naval Special Warfare's very best, and as tough as they come. That week, the Navy football team honored him at the Army–Navy game, running onto the field with a SEAL Team 8 flag and keeping his No. 13 jersey on the sideline.

He left behind his wife, Megan, and their five children.

The US Navy's newest class of warship carries a name worth knowing. The lead ship of its new Landing Ship Medium program will be the USS McClung, named for Marine Corps Major Megan McClung.

She was a public affairs officer, a Naval Academy graduate, and a marathoner known for her toughness and her motto: "Be bold. Be brief. Be gone." In December 2006, while escorting journalists through Ramadi, Iraq, her vehicle was struck by a roadside bomb. She was 34, the first female Marine officer killed in Iraq, and the first female Naval Academy graduate to die in combat.

The ship that bears her name is built for the future of Marine warfare: a small, beachable landing ship, around 4,000 tons, designed to carry Marines and gear from island to island across the Pacific. It is meant to be the backbone of a new strategy to disperse small Marine units across the first island chain to counter China.

The program has been troubled, with costs so high the Navy ended up buying a Dutch design to afford it. But whatever happens in the shipyards, the name on the hull will carry its own weight. Be bold. Be brief. Be gone.

In 1978, an 11-year-old kid sent hand-drawn missile blueprints to the Pentagon—and instead of tossing them in the trash, the Office of Naval Research gave him an official, deadpan engineering breakdown.

The Navy’s Patent Counsel actually took the time to review the submission:

The Concept: A winged, ramjet-powered missile armed with a nuclear warhead, machine guns, and sub-missiles.

The Navy's Debrief: They politely explained that ramjets require a booster to hit supersonic speed before ignition, pointed out that oversized wings create too much drag at hypersonic velocity, and noted that the Army was already testing clustered sub-munitions.

The Verdict: The Navy formally declined to adopt the platform, but enclosed real unclassified research on solid-fuel ramjet missiles so the kid could study up.

That’s how you handle curious minds. No condescension, just cold aerospace physics and encouragement from the Fleet.

Imagine pitching nuclear-armed, ramjet-driven micro-missiles from your bedroom floor and getting a typed letter back from the Chief of Naval Research. Elite era.

The Canadian Armed Forces' new BACS vest isn't just inspired by Australia's TBAS V4.5. It's a direct variant of it. Both are made by Australian Defence Apparel, which is owned by Logistik Unicorp, the company supplying the Canadian contract.

The system will be issued with a large suite of pouches, NP Aerospace plates (believed to be their III+ ICW plate), a chest rig system, and two different styles of combat belt. The plates, vest, and load carriage are built to work together as one system, instead of the mix of components soldiers have been piecing together for years.

For many Canadian soldiers, who have spent years buying their own plate carriers and pouches to replace issued gear, this could finally be a real step forward. The real test will be how it holds up in the field.

Operators from the Army's SMU in Mogadishu, Somalia, in 1993. They deployed as part of Task Force Ranger alongside the 75th Ranger Regiment and the 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment, with the mission of capturing the leadership of Mohamed Farrah Aidid's militia.

On October 3, 1993, a daylight raid in the heart of the city turned into one of the most intense firefights involving American forces since Vietnam. After two Black Hawks were shot down, the men on the ground fought through the night to reach the crash sites and protect the survivors. Two of the SMU's snipers, Master Sgt. Gary Gordon and Sgt. 1st Class Randy Shughart, volunteered to be inserted at the second crash site to protect the wounded crew. They held off the enemy until they were overwhelmed, and both were posthumously awarded the Medal of Honor, the first since the Vietnam War.

Eighteen Americans were killed in the battle, and dozens more were wounded. More than three decades later, Mogadishu remains a defining chapter for the special operations community and a reminder of what the men on the ground were willing to give for each other.

Never forget.

“WE WERE STACKING SO MANY BODIES THAT PATROLS HAD TO GO OUT TO MOVE THEM OFF OUR FIELDS OF FIRE.” — Marine Raider Cody Alford on the Battle of Fallujah on The Shawn Ryan Show.

In one of the most intense firsthand accounts of modern urban warfare ever recorded on The Shawn Ryan Show, former Marine Raider and Scout Sniper Cody Alford broke down the brutal house-to-house meatgrinder of Operation Phantom Fury—and the terrifying out-of-body experience he suffered after taking an insurgent sniper bullet directly to the helmet.

In his own words:

“The night prior to going in, my platoon commander walks in and says, ‘Everyone is going to write their death letter.’

I’m 18 years old, sitting there thinking: What do you even write? I wrote a letter to my girlfriend, wrote one to my parents, turned them over to the platoon commander, and that’s when I knew shit was real.

In Fallujah, the brutality of what we were up against was beyond comprehension. The human shields, the mutilations, the sheer volume of combat. We were stacking so many bodies that we had to send patrols out into the street just to drag bodies out of the way because they were blocking our fields of fire.

I remember stepping behind a window frame, slamming in a fresh magazine, and as soon as I pop out to shoot, everything goes black.

A profound exhale left my body, and I hit the deck. That’s when I had this out-of-body experience. It was like a video game glitch—a top-down view looking down at the entire scene. I could see the fighters across the street. I could see my own body lying still. I could see my point man still firing. I saw this blinding light, thinking: I’m f**king dead.

Then suddenly, I got sucked back into my body. I came to curled up in a fetal position with my buddy kicking my leg shouting, ‘Wake up! We thought you were dead!’

The bullet had hit me flush in the helmet.”

The Second Battle of Fallujah stands as the bloodiest, most relentless urban combat the U.S. Marine Corps has fought since the Battle of Huế City in 1968.

Drop a salute in the comments for Cody Alford and every veteran who cleared buildings in Fallujah.

Florida Swamp Phase: Navigating waterborne insertions and ambush scenarios through the dense waterways of coastal Florida, evaluating leadership while completely exhausted.

Bridging Ground & Space Domains: While Guardians manage satellite constellations, space domain awareness, and missile warning architectures, Reynolds demonstrated the vital importance of space professionals understanding the tactical realities and friction faced by frontline ground combat units.

SURROUNDED BY 300 TALIBAN AT COP KEATING, WOUNDED STAFF SGT. RALLIED COUNTERATTACK: CLINTON ROMESHA’S STAND FOR HIS MEN

At dawn on October 3, 2009, roughly 50 American soldiers defending Combat Outpost Keating—a remote, indefensible base situated at the bottom of a steep valley in eastern Afghanistan’s Nuristan Province—woke to a coordinated ambush by more than 300 heavily armed Taliban fighters raining down fire from the surrounding high ground.

During what became known as the Battle of Kamdesh, Section Leader Staff Sgt. Clinton Romesha of Bravo Troop, 3-61 Cavalry, 4th Brigade Combat Team, 4th Infantry Division, orchestrated a legendary defense recognized with the nation's highest military decoration, as documented by the U.S. Army and the Congressional Medal of Honor Society.

Gallantry Under Overwhelming Fire
According to his official Medal of Honor citation, Romesha’s actions prevented the outpost from being completely overrun:

Leading Through the Breach: After shrapnel from an RPG blast wounded his neck, shoulder, and arm, Romesha refused medical evacuation, immediately taking charge of the tactical counter-effort and moving through relentless direct machine-gun fire to rally isolated defenders.

Neutralizing High-Ground Positions: Operating without cover, Romesha utilized an array of weapons—firing an M4 carbine, taking up a fallen comrade’s sniper rifle, and employing an AT4 rocket launcher—to eliminate multiple enemy fighting positions and machine-gun bunkers.

Directing Devastating Close Air Support: Under sustained sniper fire, he calibrated target coordinates for incoming F-15E Strike Eagles, B-1B Lancers, and AH-64 Apache gunships, bringing ordnance dangerously close to friendly positions to decimate advancing Taliban waves.

The Stand for Fallen Brothers: As enemy fighters breached the perimeter, Romesha assembled a volunteer team of five soldiers, leading a push across 100 meters of exposed ground to recover the bodies of fallen teammates and secure the ammunition point so no American was left behind.

Eight American heroes made the ultimate sacrifice that day defending COP Keating: Staff Sgt. Justin Gallegos, Sgt. Christopher Griffin, Sgt. Joshua Kirk, Sgt. Michael Scusa, Spc. Stephan Mace, Spc. Kevin Thomson, Sgt. Vernon Martin, and Sgt. Joshua Hardt.

“OFF-DUTY AT AN OKINAWA GAS STATION, A U.S. MARINE HEARD A CRASH AND SPRANG INTO ACTION.”

On October 15, 2026, U.S. Marine Corps Sergeant Jacob L. Lyons had stopped at a gas station in Uruma, Okinawa, Japan, when the violent sound of a two-vehicle collision shattered the evening quiet.

He didn't hesitate. Sprinting toward the mangled wreckage, the off-duty Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) technician with the 9th Engineer Support Battalion (Combat Logistics Regiment 37, 3rd Marine Logistics Group) found an elderly Japanese woman trapped inside her car, pinned hard against the steering wheel, in severe pain and distress.

What happened next represents the best of the American military community overseas:

Freeing the Trapped Driver: Lyons forced open the passenger-side door and, teaming up with a local Japanese bystander, manually forced the driver's seat rearward to relieve the crushing pressure on her chest and give her room to breathe.

Immediate Trauma Care: Lyons’ wife a former U.S. Navy Corpsman rushed over with another bystander to contact emergency dispatchers, providing immediate first aid and comforting the terrified driver through the language barrier.

Securing the Scene: Recognizing the danger of secondary collisions on the active roadway, Lyons stepped out into traffic, directing vehicles away from the wreckage and maintaining a clear access lane for incoming Japanese police and ambulances.

On October 23, 2026, at Camp Kinser, Colonel Robert Gerbracht presented Sergeant Lyons with the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal for his swift life-saving actions.

“In a moment when another person's well-being was at stake, Sergeant Lyons did not hesitate,” said Col. Gerbracht. “He stepped forward with compassion, calm, and courage to help a member of our Okinawan community in need. His actions are a powerful reflection of our Marine Corps values and of the responsibility we carry as neighbors, partners, and guests in Japan.”

For Lyons, the motivation was simple:

“It was the right thing to do, not just as a Marine, but as a good person. Someone was in need and I was able to help, so I needed to.”

Tu Lam was born in Saigon in December 1974, just months before the city fell. He kept that promise. Lam joined the Army and spent 23 years in uniform, 20 of them as a Green Beret, deploying to conflicts around the world. His career also took him into the Army's SMU community as an augmentee, and he retired as a Master Sergeant.

After leaving the military, he founded Ronin Tactics, built on his combat experience, his lifelong study of martial arts, and the samurai code of bushido. He became the inspiration for the character Ronin in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, co-hosted Forged in Fire: Knife or Death, and told his story in his memoir, "The Way of Ronin."

From a refugee boat to the Special Forces Regiment, few journeys say more about what America can mean.

“THE POINT MAN FELL AT THE DOORWAY. HE CHARGED IN ANYWAY.” How Navy SEAL Edward Byers Shielded an American Hostage with His Own Body.

On the night of December 8, 2012, a hostage rescue force from SEAL Team 6 inserted into the rugged mountains of eastern Afghanistan on a mission with zero room for error: rescue American physician Dr. Dilip Joseph, who had been kidnapped by Taliban militants and was hours away from being smuggled across the border into Pakistan.

After a grueling four-hour foot patrol through steep terrain, the team reached the isolated target compound in Laghman Province:

As the team approached, an armed sentry alerted fighters inside. Point man Chief Petty Officer Nicolas Checque breached the entrance and was immediately struck by point-blank AK-47 fire and mortally wounded.

Without a second of hesitation, Senior Chief Edward Byers pushed directly through the doorway—the deadly "fatal funnel." He ripped down heavy blankets blocking the threshold, sprinted into the darkened room, and neutralized an armed Taliban fighter.

 Tackling another insurgent to the floor, Byers heard a voice speaking English. Spotting Dr. Joseph in the corner, Byers immediately threw his own body across the doctor, using his plate carrier and physical weight to shield the hostage from heavy incoming gunfire.

 While pinning himself over Dr. Joseph to absorb any stray rounds, Byers noticed another armed guard within arm's reach. With his bare hand, Byers grabbed the insurgent by the throat, pinning him against the wall until his teammates could eliminate the threat.

Dr. Joseph was successfully extracted alive and uninjured. Chief Petty Officer Nicolas Checque made the ultimate sacrifice that night and was posthumously awarded the Navy Cross.

On February 29, 2016, Edward Byers was presented the Medal of Honor, becoming only the sixth Navy SEAL in history to receive the nation’s highest military award for valor.

TRAPPED INSIDE A 1,000-DEGREE INFERNO FOR 90 SECONDS. In March 2001, Phoenix Police Officer Jason Schechterle was stopped at a red light in his Crown Victoria cruiser when a vehicle traveling over 115 mph rear-ended him, rupturing the fuel tank and igniting a blinding fireball. Trapped inside with crumpled doors, he survived fourth-degree burns across 40% of his body, endured over 50 surgeries, and built an unbreakable life out of the ashes.

“I was trapped in a cage of fire for a minute and a half. When I finally woke up from a two-and-a-half-month coma, my face was gone, my hands were severely damaged, and my life as I knew it had vanished. But tragedy doesn't define who you are—your response to it does. There is nothing in this world as powerful as a made-up mind.”

— Officer Jason Schechterle, Phoenix Police Department & Author of Burning Shield

The Incident & The 90-Second Rescue
The 115 MPH Collision: Stopped at an intersection on Thomas Road in Phoenix, Arizona, Officer Jason Schechterle’s patrol vehicle was rear-ended at highway speeds by a driver who had suffered a medical seizure behind the wheel.

 The severe impact crushed the Crown Victoria’s rear crumple zone into the fuel tank, sparking an immediate 1,000-degree gasoline fire that engulfed the passenger cabin and jammed the doors shut.

Phoenix Fire Captain Gary West was nearby when the crash occurred. Armed with only a small dry-chemical extinguisher, he fought through intense heat, forced open the mangled door frame, and pulled Schechterle from the burning cockpit with seconds to spare.

 Schechterle sustained devastating fourth-degree burns across more than 40% of his body, losing his ears, nose, eyelids, and facial skin. Placed into a medically induced coma for two and a half months, he underwent more than 50 surgeries to reconstruct his features and restore eyesight.

Demonstrating extraordinary resilience, Schechterle returned to work with the Phoenix Police Department, authored his autobiography Burning Shield, and became an internationally renowned keynote speaker on overcoming life-altering adversity.

Key Lessons on Resilience & Overcoming Adversity
Focusing on the Response, Not the Circumstance: Pain and trauma are inevitable, but victimhood is a choice. Reframing catastrophic injury into a platform for service enables long-term psychological recovery.

Winning the Internal Battle: Recovery from severe physical trauma is primarily cognitive. Rebuilding daily discipline and maintaining positive internal dialogue prevents despair from taking root.

The Power of First Responder Brotherhood: Schechterle’s survival was made possible by the decisive, selfless courage of a firefighter who entered a raging vehicle fire without full protective gear to save a brother officer.

“EVIDENCE INDICATES PARTS OF THE JET BROKE OFF BEFORE IMPACT.” — Federal investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board reveal that the doomed Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, likely suffered an in-flight structural breakup at altitude, aligning with dashcam video appearing to show the aircraft plunging nose-first without its T-tail horizontal stabilizer.

“There are indications the aircraft began breaking up prior to impact. We may find parts of the aircraft some distance away from the actual impact site... We are asking anyone in the community who locates debris to contact local law enforcement immediately.”

— National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) Press Briefing in Palm Beach County

“We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence... Mayday, mayday, we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute... We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute... We’re going to crash into the ground.”

— Cockpit transmissions broadcast over Air Traffic Control frequencies moments before impact

Aerodynamic & Forensic Breakdown
The In-Flight Breakup Finding: During their initial media briefing in Palm Beach County, NTSB investigators confirmed that the Learjet 60 began shedding components prior to striking the ground, officially expanding the search radius across residential neighborhoods miles away from the primary impact crater.

The Missing Horizontal Stabilizer: Close-up frame analysis of civilian dashcam footage captured seconds before impact appears to show the aircraft's T-tail fuselage cleanly sheared off, missing the entire horizontal stabilizer and elevator assembly that controls aircraft pitch.

Why Loss of the Stabilizer is Fatal: On swept-wing, T-tail jets like the Learjet 60, the horizontal stabilizer generates continuous downward aerodynamic force to counter the natural forward center of gravity. If the stabilizer separates due to severe structural flutter, pitch trim runaway, or aerodynamic over-stress, the aircraft immediately lawn-darts into a near-vertical terminal dive that is physically impossible to pull out of, regardless of pilot yoke input.

The Escalating Mayday Telemetry: Flight tracking telemetry and ATC recordings show the crew encountered severe weather and icing while climbing through 8,700 feet. The aircraft suddenly entered an uncontrollable overspeed condition, with vertical descent rates accelerating from 10,000 FPM past 32,000 FPM before the violent ground collision.

Key Investigation Priorities for the NTSB
Locating the Empennage Components: Ground teams are prioritizing the recovery of tail structure fragments, elevator control horns, and pitch trim actuators to determine whether failure was aerodynamic, mechanical, or structural.

Analyzing Trim Jackscrew Position: Recovery crews will inspect the horizontal stabilizer trim actuator jackscrew to determine if an uncommanded runaway pitch condition preceded the structural separation.

Evaluating Atmospheric Stress & Icing: Meteorologists and investigators are analyzing weather radar data to evaluate whether severe convective turbulence or structural ice accumulation induced catastrophic aerodynamic loading at cruise altitude.

When the Civil War broke out, Mary Walker wasn't asking for permission. She was already a doctor, one of the very few women in America who could say that back in 1855. The Army told her women couldn't serve as surgeons. So she showed up anyway and worked for free.

She treated wounded Union soldiers in field hospitals, often close to the fighting. She'd cross into dangerous ground to care for civilians too, and in April 1864 that cost her. Confederate troops captured her and accused her of being a spy. She spent four months locked up in Castle Thunder prison in Richmond before she was traded back in a prisoner exchange.

In November 1865, President Andrew Johnson awarded her the Medal of Honor.

But her story didn't end neatly. In 1917, the government tightened the rules and took the medal back from her and hundreds of others. Mary's answer? She refused to return it. She wore it every single day until she died in 1919.

It took almost 60 more years, but in 1977 President Jimmy Carter restored her medal.

To this day, she is the only woman ever to receive the Medal of Honor.

She was stubborn, fearless, and way ahead of her time. And she never once backed down.

Rest easy, Dr. Walker. 🇺🇸

Prisoners of war have tried everything to escape, but few plans were as patient — or as strange — as Benjamin Purcell's. Held in a North Vietnamese prison camp, the Army officer spent months secretly drilling tiny holes into his cell door, a little at a time, always watching for the guards. His early-warning system was a chicken he had trained to react whenever anyone approached.

He would not see freedom until 1973. He retired as a colonel, carrying one of the most remarkable escape stories of the Vietnam War: no tools, no help, just patience, nerve, and a chicken.

For decades, a typical U.S. Navy carrier strike group deployment lasted six to seven months. According to naval leadership reports, returning to predictable seven-month deployment schedules could still be several years away as the fleet struggles to balance global commitments with limited ready ships.

Why Carrier Tours Keep Getting Extended:

 Continuous combat operations in the Red Sea countering Houthi missile and drone swarms have forced strike groups including the USS Gerald R. Ford (326 days at sea) and the USS Abraham Lincoln (over 320 days) into historic, repeated deployment extensions.

With commercial and naval shipyards overwhelmed by maintenance delays, fresh replacement carriers and guided-missile destroyers often aren't ready to relieve ships on station, forcing deployed crews to stay underway longer.

 Prolonged separations put intense psychological strain on military families, fueling concerns over burnout, mental health, and reenlistment rates among junior enlisted personnel.

Fleet Forces Command leadership notes that until the Navy has enough ship capacity and cleared maintenance backlogs, extended 10-to-11-month deployments will remain an expectation rather than an exception.

In 1978, an 11-year-old kid sent hand-drawn missile blueprints to the Pentagon—and instead of tossing them in the trash, the Office of Naval Research gave him an official, deadpan engineering breakdown.

The Navy’s Patent Counsel actually took the time to review the submission:

The Concept: A winged, ramjet-powered missile armed with a nuclear warhead, machine guns, and sub-missiles.

The Navy's Debrief: They politely explained that ramjets require a booster to hit supersonic speed before ignition, pointed out that oversized wings create too much drag at hypersonic velocity, and noted that the Army was already testing clustered sub-munitions.

The Verdict: The Navy formally declined to adopt the platform, but enclosed real unclassified research on solid-fuel ramjet missiles so the kid could study up.

That’s how you handle curious minds. No condescension, just cold aerospace physics and encouragement from the Fleet.

Imagine pitching nuclear-armed, ramjet-driven micro-missiles from your bedroom floor and getting a typed letter back from the Chief of Naval Research. Elite era.

“WE WERE STACKING SO MANY BODIES THAT PATROLS HAD TO GO OUT TO MOVE THEM OFF OUR FIELDS OF FIRE.” — Marine Raider Cody Alford on the Battle of Fallujah on The Shawn Ryan Show.

In one of the most intense firsthand accounts of modern urban warfare ever recorded on The Shawn Ryan Show, former Marine Raider and Scout Sniper Cody Alford broke down the brutal house-to-house meatgrinder of Operation Phantom Fury—and the terrifying out-of-body experience he suffered after taking an insurgent sniper bullet directly to the helmet.

In his own words:

“The night prior to going in, my platoon commander walks in and says, ‘Everyone is going to write their death letter.’

I’m 18 years old, sitting there thinking: What do you even write? I wrote a letter to my girlfriend, wrote one to my parents, turned them over to the platoon commander, and that’s when I knew shit was real.

In Fallujah, the brutality of what we were up against was beyond comprehension. The human shields, the mutilations, the sheer volume of combat. We were stacking so many bodies that we had to send patrols out into the street just to drag bodies out of the way because they were blocking our fields of fire.

I remember stepping behind a window frame, slamming in a fresh magazine, and as soon as I pop out to shoot, everything goes black.

A profound exhale left my body, and I hit the deck. That’s when I had this out-of-body experience. It was like a video game glitch—a top-down view looking down at the entire scene. I could see the fighters across the street. I could see my own body lying still. I could see my point man still firing. I saw this blinding light, thinking: I’m f**king dead.

Then suddenly, I got sucked back into my body. I came to curled up in a fetal position with my buddy kicking my leg shouting, ‘Wake up! We thought you were dead!’

The bullet had hit me flush in the helmet.”

The Second Battle of Fallujah stands as the bloodiest, most relentless urban combat the U.S. Marine Corps has fought since the Battle of Huế City in 1968.

SURROUNDED BY 300 TALIBAN AT COP KEATING, WOUNDED STAFF SGT. RALLIED COUNTERATTACK: CLINTON ROMESHA’S STAND FOR HIS MEN

At dawn on October 3, 2009, roughly 50 American soldiers defending Combat Outpost Keating—a remote, indefensible base situated at the bottom of a steep valley in eastern Afghanistan’s Nuristan Province—woke to a coordinated ambush by more than 300 heavily armed Taliban fighters raining down fire from the surrounding high ground.

During what became known as the Battle of Kamdesh, Section Leader Staff Sgt. Clinton Romesha of Bravo Troop, 3-61 Cavalry, 4th Brigade Combat Team, 4th Infantry Division, orchestrated a legendary defense recognized with the nation's highest military decoration, as documented by the U.S. Army and the Congressional Medal of Honor Society.

Gallantry Under Overwhelming Fire
According to his official Medal of Honor citation, Romesha’s actions prevented the outpost from being completely overrun:

Leading Through the Breach: After shrapnel from an RPG blast wounded his neck, shoulder, and arm, Romesha refused medical evacuation, immediately taking charge of the tactical counter-effort and moving through relentless direct machine-gun fire to rally isolated defenders.

Neutralizing High-Ground Positions: Operating without cover, Romesha utilized an array of weapons—firing an M4 carbine, taking up a fallen comrade’s sniper rifle, and employing an AT4 rocket launcher—to eliminate multiple enemy fighting positions and machine-gun bunkers.

Directing Devastating Close Air Support: Under sustained sniper fire, he calibrated target coordinates for incoming F-15E Strike Eagles, B-1B Lancers, and AH-64 Apache gunships, bringing ordnance dangerously close to friendly positions to decimate advancing Taliban waves.

The Stand for Fallen Brothers: As enemy fighters breached the perimeter, Romesha assembled a volunteer team of five soldiers, leading a push across 100 meters of exposed ground to recover the bodies of fallen teammates and secure the ammunition point so no American was left behind.

Eight American heroes made the ultimate sacrifice that day defending COP Keating: Staff Sgt. Justin Gallegos, Sgt. Christopher Griffin, Sgt. Joshua Kirk, Sgt. Michael Scusa, Spc. Stephan Mace, Spc. Kevin Thomson, Sgt. Vernon Martin, and Sgt. Joshua Hardt.

“OFF-DUTY AT AN OKINAWA GAS STATION, A U.S. MARINE HEARD A CRASH AND SPRANG INTO ACTION.”

On October 15, 2026, U.S. Marine Corps Sergeant Jacob L. Lyons had stopped at a gas station in Uruma, Okinawa, Japan, when the violent sound of a two-vehicle collision shattered the evening quiet.

He didn't hesitate. Sprinting toward the mangled wreckage, the off-duty Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) technician with the 9th Engineer Support Battalion (Combat Logistics Regiment 37, 3rd Marine Logistics Group) found an elderly Japanese woman trapped inside her car, pinned hard against the steering wheel, in severe pain and distress.

What happened next represents the best of the American military community overseas:

Freeing the Trapped Driver: Lyons forced open the passenger-side door and, teaming up with a local Japanese bystander, manually forced the driver's seat rearward to relieve the crushing pressure on her chest and give her room to breathe.

Immediate Trauma Care: Lyons’ wife a former U.S. Navy Corpsman rushed over with another bystander to contact emergency dispatchers, providing immediate first aid and comforting the terrified driver through the language barrier.

Securing the Scene: Recognizing the danger of secondary collisions on the active roadway, Lyons stepped out into traffic, directing vehicles away from the wreckage and maintaining a clear access lane for incoming Japanese police and ambulances.

On October 23, 2026, at Camp Kinser, Colonel Robert Gerbracht presented Sergeant Lyons with the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal for his swift life-saving actions.

“In a moment when another person's well-being was at stake, Sergeant Lyons did not hesitate,” said Col. Gerbracht. “He stepped forward with compassion, calm, and courage to help a member of our Okinawan community in need. His actions are a powerful reflection of our Marine Corps values and of the responsibility we carry as neighbors, partners, and guests in Japan.”

For Lyons, the motivation was simple:

“It was the right thing to do, not just as a Marine, but as a good person. Someone was in need and I was able to help, so I needed to.”

Singlaub never sought the spotlight. He just ran the hardest command of the war, in the shadows, and brought as many of his men home as he could.
